variants.name: Live signal: KOSPI, margin credit, ETF share, KTB 10Y trend
US 10Y trend in place of the KTB trend
Local flows only (KOSPI, margin, ETF share)

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each KOFIA close. Hedged = KTB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks.

src: US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Naver Finance: KOSPI and ETF weekly charts (KODEX 국고채30년액티브 439870, KODEX 200 069500). KOFIA: 10Y KTB final quote; freesis margin credit balance (신용공여 잔고) and investor deposits (투자자예탁금). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: 30Y KTB ETF turnover share: 4-week avg minus 26-week avg

notes.headline: Stocks down, bonds up: KOSPI −18% in four weeks, 10Y KTB −36bp, of which about −15bp tracks US Treasuries and −20bp is Korea's own rotation. Signal +1.75: bond rally
notes.now: Leveraged equity money is still leaving: margin credit fell another KRW 1.1tn this week to 29.1tn (peak 38.5tn on Jun 19) and broker deposits dropped KRW 12tn in four weeks to 88.7tn. All three flow and momentum parts point to bonds (KOSPI 4-week z −1.7, margin −2.0, KTB 10Y trend −2.4); the bond ETF part adds little because 30Y KTB ETF turnover is tiny next to KODEX 200. Treasuries explain part of the move but not most of it: the US 10Y fell 26bp over the same four weeks, and at the current weekly beta of 0.59 that accounts for about −15bp of the KTB's −36bp, leaving −20bp of Korea-specific rally. That local piece is what the signal is built to call, and it is where its record is best: traded against β × US 10Y, rally calls were right 64% of the time and sell-off calls 69% (46% and 57% outright), with a Sharpe of 1.26 against 0.92. Day to day, KTBs take about 0.46bp of every 1bp overnight Treasury move (R² 0.16 over the last year) and price it the same morning; there is no follow-through the next day. The KTB 10Y now yields 97bp less than the US 10Y, the widest gap in a year, so Korea has already outperformed a lot. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: the rotation still favours KTBs over Treasuries rather than outright duration. With the BOK leaning to a November hike and US yields near 5%, a beta-hedged position (long KTB 10Y against about 0.5–0.6 × US 10Y) keeps the local view while cutting the US risk that has driven the biggest drawdowns.
notes.flip: The signal needs KOSPI to recover about 8–10% over four weeks with margin credit rising again; it would then fall back through +0.5 within two to three weeks. On the US side, watch the beta: if the 60-day beta climbs back above 0.6 (as in early 2026), Treasuries dominate again and the hedge ratio should rise with it; a firm October CPI and a November BOK hike would turn the KTB-trend part against bonds even if stocks stay weak.
phases: KOSPI 2,400–2,900 and 10Y 3.1–4.2%. The signal was mostly neutral, and its few calls were driven by global yields rather than local rotation.
The BOK cut, the 10Y fell to about 2.7% and KOSPI drifted. Bond-rally readings around December 2024 worked.

KOSPI ran from about 2,800 to 7,500 by May 2026 on chip exports, and margin credit doubled to the high 30s (KRW tn). The signal read sell-off for most of the year while the 10Y rose from 2.8% to 3.9%. This was the signal's best stretch.
Peak, hikes and a false rally call
KOSPI peaked at 9,052 on Jun 19, then cracked. The signal called a bond rally, but the BOK hiked in July and August and the 10Y rose 35bp to a 4.54% high in September. Rotation lost to policy.

KOSPI fell 18% in four weeks on AI-earnings doubts and foreign selling, and the 10Y fell about 40bp to 4.01%. The signal has read bond rally since Oct 8, and this time it has worked: the 10Y is down 39bp since the call.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows. Margin credit and deposits come from KOFIA freesis daily statistics. The bond ETF share uses KODEX 국고채30년액티브 (439870), whose turnover is under 1% of KODEX 200's, so that part is weak. US Treasury levels are official par yields at the New York close, aligned to the last close before each KOFIA close, so the back-test never uses a US move the KTB market had not yet seen. The back-test starts in 2023 and covers one full equity cycle; most of the gain came after March 2025 (hedged Sharpe 1.89 vs 0.43 before), so treat the signal as a regime gauge alongside BOK pricing, not as a stand-alone trade. Adding the US 10Y trend as a fifth input made the signal worse (Sharpe 0.41 outright, 0.81 hedged), so Treasuries are used as the hedge and the attribution, not as a signal input.
